newsitem.title: USA: US cites gains in opening Japan car market.
newsitem.headline: US cites gains in opening Japan car market.

text.p: Significant gains have been made in opening Japan's car and auto parts markets to more foreign products, U.S. trade officials said Tuesday.
Officials gave reporters an upbeat assessment of the 1995 car and parts trade agreement with Japan ahead of a formal review of the trade pact this week in San Francisco.
"By virtually all measures the agreement has been a success," a U.S. trade official said.
"Significant gains have been made in opening Japan's auto markets, and we will continue to see those gains over the course of the auto agreement," the official said.
Officials said that exports of cars to Japan from North America by the Big Three automakers are up 40 percent so far this year over the same period last year.

U.S. and Japanese trade officials will meet Wednesday and Thursday in San Francisco to review the year-old accord on cars and car parts. Canadian, Australian and European union representatives will join in on the discussions, U.S. trade officials said.

American manufacturers have expressed concern that an insufficient number of new dealerships have been signed up to sell American brand cars and have also expressed concern about the pace of deregulation of the auto parts market.

But overall, U.S. officials say the trade agreement has been a success and some elements have exceeded expectations. They specificially cited the sale of U.S.-brand shocks and struts, which they said were up 250 percent so far this year, far exceeding expectations.
